section_summary: This section concerns Japanese public vessels visiting U.S. ports in 1939 and early 1940. It records U.S. decisions on cargo and customs rules, a customs courtesy incident at Hilo, and a Yokohama consul’s report on Japanese vessel calls and prior authorization. Much of the section tracks repeated changes to the transport Iro’s proposed visits to Los Angeles and Hilo.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department reply on cargo carried by foreign public vessels
subfiles.about: Commerce agrees to instruct customs field offices to require foreign public vessels to comply with cargo laws.
subfiles.summary: Commerce agrees that customs courtesies do not excuse foreign public vessels from cargo requirements. Field offices will warn commanders and promptly report any refusal to comply.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Hilo customs incident letter
subfiles.about: Treasury forwards its response to a customs officer’s encounter with a sentry aboard a Japanese naval vessel.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Treasury’s letter to the Honolulu customs collector about the Hilo incident.

subfiles.title: Treasury guidance on customs courtesies for foreign naval vessels
subfiles.about: Treasury closes the Hilo sentry incident and explains customary treatment of visiting foreign naval vessels.
subfiles.summary: Accepts the Japanese consul’s regrets and describes welcoming officers, permitting crew to land, and avoiding vessel inspections.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy note changing Iro’s Hilo visit
subfiles.about: The transport Iro proposes to visit Hilo on February 6, 1940, while retaining its Los Angeles schedule.
subfiles.summary: Announces Iro’s revised Hilo date and says its Los Angeles date is unchanged.

subfiles.title: State Department acknowledgment of Iro’s Hilo schedule
subfiles.about: State acknowledges the revised Hilo date and says federal departments have been informed.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Iro’s February 6 Hilo visit and the then unchanged Los Angeles date.

subfiles.title: Notice to Agriculture of Iro’s revised Hilo visit
subfiles.about: State advises Agriculture that Iro’s Hilo visit has moved to February 6, 1940.
subfiles.summary: Reports the changed Hilo date; Los Angeles remains scheduled for crude petroleum loading.

subfiles.title: Notice to Interior of Iro’s revised Hilo visit
subfiles.about: State advises Interior that Iro’s Hilo visit has moved to February 6, 1940.
subfiles.summary: Reports the changed Hilo date and unchanged Los Angeles visit.

subfiles.title: Notice to Labor of Iro’s revised Hilo visit

subfiles.summary: Reports the changed Hilo date and unchanged Los Angeles visit.

subfiles.title: Notice to Navy of Iro’s revised Hilo visit

subfiles.summary: Reports the changed Hilo date and unchanged Los Angeles visit.

subfiles.title: Notice to Treasury of Iro’s revised Hilo visit
subfiles.about: State advises Treasury that Iro’s Hilo visit has moved to February 6, 1940.
subfiles.summary: Reports the changed Hilo date and unchanged Los Angeles visit.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on informing Yokohama of authorization practice
subfiles.about: A division note suggests telling the Yokohama consul that diplomatic missions seek permission for public-vessel visits.
subfiles.summary: Suggests an instruction explaining State’s authorization practice to the consul at Yokohama.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs digest of Yokohama despatch 574
subfiles.about: The division summarizes Japanese public-vessel calls and the consul’s question about reciprocal authorization.
subfiles.summary: Notes sixteen voyages in 1938–39, many by tankers or training ships, and the consul’s practice of requiring advance authorization only for closed U.S. ports.

subfiles.title: Despatch 574: Calls of Japanese Public Vessels at United States Ports
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul at Yokohama
subfiles.about: The consul tabulates Japanese public-vessel voyages and questions differing U.S. and Japanese prior-authorization practices.
subfiles.summary: Boyce counts sixteen voyages and thirty U.S. port calls from January 1938 through October 1939. Training ships and naval tankers predominate; tankers appear to carry oil from Los Angeles for the Japanese Navy. He notes frequent calls at Honolulu and Hilo and says his consulate seeks prior U.S. authorization only for closed ports, whereas Japan requires it for American public vessels visiting open Japanese ports.

subfiles.title: State reply to Boyce on authorization of Japanese vessel visits
subfiles.to: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul at Yokohama
subfiles.about: State explains that Japanese diplomatic requests had preceded the vessel visits listed in Boyce’s despatch.
subfiles.summary: Cites a circular requesting diplomatic notice of foreign public-vessel visits. State says the Japanese Embassy sought permission in each case and that State consults interested federal authorities before replying.

subfiles.title: Labor acknowledgment of Iro’s revised Hilo visit
subfiles.about: Labor acknowledges Iro’s new Hilo date and informs its Honolulu office.
subfiles.summary: Confirms that Honolulu immigration officials are being told of Iro’s February 6 Hilo visit.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment of Iro’s revised Hilo visit
subfiles.about: Treasury informs the Honolulu customs collector of Iro’s revised Hilo date.
subfiles.summary: Confirms notification to the Honolulu customs collector.

subfiles.title: War Department acknowledgment of Iro’s revised Hilo visit
subfiles.about: War forwards Iro’s changed Hilo schedule to the Hawaiian Department.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the revised date and informs the Hawaiian Department’s commanding general.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of report on scrap tin aboard Erimo
subfiles.about: Treasury forwards the Honolulu collector’s finding on scrap tin loaded aboard the Japanese naval tanker Erimo.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a finding that crushed used cans fall outside the cited tin-plate-scrap definition.

subfiles.title: Honolulu customs report on scrap tin aboard Erimo
subfiles.about: The collector determines whether Erimo’s cargo meets the State Department definition of tin-plate scrap.
subfiles.summary: Finds that the cargo was crushed used tin cans and outside the cited definition.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy correction of Iro’s Los Angeles date
subfiles.about: The ambassador corrects an earlier statement and moves Iro’s Los Angeles visit to January 22, 1940.
subfiles.summary: Sets Los Angeles for January 22 and retains February 6 for Hilo.

subfiles.title: Notice to California governor of Iro’s Los Angeles change
subfiles.about: State reports Iro’s proposed Los Angeles arrival on January 22, 1940.
subfiles.summary: Advises the governor of Iro’s revised Los Angeles date.

subfiles.title: Notice to Treasury of Iro’s Los Angeles change
subfiles.about: State reports Iro’s January 22 Los Angeles date and unchanged February 6 Hilo date.
subfiles.summary: Advises Treasury of the revised Los Angeles visit.

subfiles.summary: Advises War of the revised Los Angeles visit.

subfiles.title: State acknowledgment of corrected Iro schedule
subfiles.about: State acknowledges Iro’s January 22 Los Angeles date and February 6 Hilo date.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the correction and says federal departments have been informed.

subfiles.title: War Department acknowledgment of Iro’s Los Angeles change
subfiles.about: War forwards Iro’s January 22 Los Angeles date to its Ninth Corps Area commander.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the change and informs the commander at the Presidio of San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment of Iro’s Los Angeles change
subfiles.about: Treasury informs the Los Angeles customs collector of Iro’s changed visit date.
subfiles.summary: Confirms notification to the Los Angeles customs collector.

subfiles.title: Navy approval of Iro’s revised port visits
subfiles.about: Navy has no objection to Iro’s revised Los Angeles and Hilo visits.
subfiles.summary: Accepts Los Angeles on January 22–26 and Hilo on February 6; local naval authorities will extend courtesies.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy note moving Iro’s Los Angeles visit to January 21
subfiles.about: Iro’s Los Angeles visit moves one day earlier, while its Hilo date remains February 6, 1940.
subfiles.summary: Announces January 21 for Los Angeles and retains February 6 for Hilo.

subfiles.title: Notice to California governor of Iro’s January 21 visit
subfiles.about: State reports Iro’s latest Los Angeles date.
subfiles.summary: Advises the governor that Iro now proposes January 21.

subfiles.title: Notice to Agriculture of Iro’s January 21 visit
subfiles.about: State reports Iro’s January 21 Los Angeles date and unchanged Hilo date.
subfiles.summary: Advises Agriculture of the latest schedule change.

subfiles.title: State acknowledgment of Iro’s January 21 Los Angeles date
subfiles.about: State acknowledges Iro’s latest schedule and says U.S. authorities have been informed.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges January 21 for Los Angeles and February 6 for Hilo.
